clue.text: Equity produces reasonable drama

parts.note: a reasonable deal is a fair one
a drama staged in a theatre is a play

explanation.surface: Actors' union Equity puts on a sensible piece of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is also the British actors' union, which feeds the theatrical surface, but here it means even-handedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is justice and even-handed treatment, the same idea as sporting decency.

clue.text: Litter gets an argument well away

parts.note: something well away is far off
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A rubbish problem leads to a quarrel a long way off.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrow is a litter of piglets, and to farrow is for a sow to give birth.

clue.text: Rouse the people with popular quote

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: A demagogue stirs up the crowd with a crowd-pleasing quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up a crowd, urging them to action, is to provoke or foment them.

clue.text: I'd clap wildly even when calm

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of the words before it are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stays serene even while applauding enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and serene, untroubled by excitement.

clue.text: Egalitarians make this claim nonetheless

definitions.meaning: people who believe in equality say everybody is equal, read literally as a phrase
an adverb meaning even so or in spite of that

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally asserts sameness, as egalitarians do, and idiomatically means however or even so.

clue.text: Spirits emerging from small opening to the Underworld

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from small

parts.note: Hades is the Greek underworld of the dead

explanation.surface: Ghosts rise out of a narrow entrance to the land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are ghosts or departed spirits in classical poetry.

clue.text: Lots of people take lots of time getting them released

definitions.text: Lots of people take lots of time getting them released

parts.note: a host is a great crowd of people
ages is a long while

explanation.surface: A large group of captives takes a long time to be freed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes captives whose release drags on; 'take' and 'getting them released' join the pieces in the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Captives held as security are people whose release is negotiated slowly.

clue.text: What couples do when convulsed with laughter

definitions.meaning: to couple things is to pair or combine them

explanation.definitionFit: To pair things is to make them twofold, and folding over in hysterics is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Is swayed alternatively to left or right

indicators.note: alternatively suggests another arrangement of the words Is swayed

explanation.surface: Someone rocks from one side to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards one side or the other rather than forwards is lateral movement.

clue.text: US intelligence men in meeting about ethnicity

indicators.note: in places the spies inside the word for the gathering

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting
the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: American spies infiltrate a gathering concerned with ethnic issues.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in terms of race, which is to say concerning ethnic origin.

clue.text: Is threatened with court action-clearly after publication

parts.note: someone sued faces a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Someone faces a lawsuit right after their book comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that has been published has been put out to the public.

clue.text: Unqualified appeal to put the Socialists in

definitions.text: appeal to put the Socialists in
definitions.meaning: a call to throw out the Conservative right wing so the left can govern

explanation.definitionFit: Total or absolute, and read as two words a cry to eject the right from power.

clue.text: Everyone comes in to cut the grass and plant

indicators.note: comes in puts the word for everyone inside the word for cutting grass

parts.note: to cut grass is to mow it
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everybody joins in the lawn-mowing and the planting.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallow is a flowering plant of the hollyhock family.

clue.text: To be acceptable security disc has to have royal cipher

parts.note: a pass is a badge or token granting entry
must means has to
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the royal monogram

explanation.surface: A security badge must bear the monarch's monogram to be valid.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, was the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II on British pillar boxes and badges.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet the required standard is to be good enough.

clue.text: A property with responsibility to tender tax

parts.note: an estate is a landed property
a duty is an obligation

explanation.surface: Owning land brings an obligation to pay up.
explanation.walkthrough: Estate duty was the British inheritance tax levied on a dead person's property.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a levy on the value of what a deceased person left, an inheritance charge.

clue.text: Related declaration of divorced status

definitions.meaning: past tense of relate, meaning told or recounted
a person saying they are separated, as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to communicate it; split as a contraction, the letters say someone is separated.

clue.text: Confessed to having been taken in

definitions.meaning: let in or received as a patient or member

explanation.definitionFit: One owns up by acknowledging guilt, and a patient taken into hospital is received.

clue.text: Casual relationships cost nothing nothing

parts.note: something that costs nothing is free
love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Fleeting affairs come with no price tag at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The doubled 'nothing' looks like a misprint; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual relationships without commitment or marriage, a phrase from the 1960s.

clue.text: The way sailors feel the absence of a stylish young lady

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
RN is the Royal Navy
to miss someone is to feel their absence

explanation.surface: Sailors pine for a fashionable girl they left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-to-date, fashionable girl of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Where animal lovers may find consolation if piqued

definitions.text: Where animal lovers may find consolation
definitions.meaning: a domestic animal as a source of comfort

explanation.definitionFit: Sulking is a fit of pique; literally the words place someone inside a companion animal.

clue.text: Choose Nicholas, one hears, to make a meal

indicators.note: one hears signals the words are said out loud

parts.note: to choose is to pick, and Nicholas is shortened to Nick

explanation.surface: Someone picks Nick to cook dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal eaten informally.

clue.text: Advanced one pound to get dhal

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling

explanation.surface: Lending a pound to buy an Indian lentil dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Dhal is the Indian dish of split pulses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal is made from split pulses of this kind.

clue.text: Stays with Jack before the 13th

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, AB being an able seaman
the Ides fell on the 13th day of most Roman months

explanation.surface: A man named Jack stays until mid-month.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain or dwell somewhere.

clue.text: Fail to get one's skates on and achieve little

definitions.text: Fail to get one's skates on
definitions.meaning: an ice rink scene read literally, skates failing to slice frozen water

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for making no impression, read literally as skates failing on frozen water.

clue.text: Beating the drum for tasteless clothes as well

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless stuff
too means also

explanation.surface: A drummer advertises gaudy clothes and more besides.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumbeat or military beat on a drum, as in a signal recalling soldiers.

clue.text: Hurry to expose devious nepotist

indicators.note: devious suggests the letters of nepotist take a crooked route into a new order

explanation.surface: Rush to unmask a scheming boss who favours relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells a driver to press the accelerator, meaning go faster.

clue.text: Daughter taking more rum must be unsteady on her feet!

parts.note: rum means odd, so more rum is odder

explanation.surface: A girl drinking extra rum will wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter shakily, as an elderly person does.

clue.text: Formalities observed by Colonel Blimp

parts.note: the rules of etiquette that a pompous old-school officer would insist on, with COL present inside

explanation.surface: A pompous old officer insists on correct etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp is a cartoon pompous British reactionary officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Official rules of correct conduct and etiquette.
